p: To reprove him, because he had committed horrible sins, and lain in the same without repentance more then a whole year.
according to thy lovingkindness: As his sins were many and great, so he requires that God would give him the feeling of his excellent and abundant mercies.
throughly from mine iniquity: My sins strike so fast in me, that I have need of some singular kind of washing.
acknowledge my transgressions: My conscience accuses me so, that I can have no rest till I am reconciled.
speakest: When you give sentence against sinners, they must confess you to be just, and themselves sinners.
desirest truth in the inward parts: He confesses that God who loves pureness of heart, may justly destroy man, who by nature is a sinner much more him whom he had instructed in his heavenly wisdom.
joy and gladness: He means God's comfortable mercies toward repentant sinners.
bones which thou hast broken may: By the bones he understands all strength of soul and body, which by cares and mourning are consumed.
Create in me a clean heart: He confesses that when God's Spirit is cold in us, to have it again revived, is as a new creation.
free spirit: Which may assure me that I am drawn out of the slavery of sin.
ways: He promises to endeavour that others by his example may turn to God.
bloodguiltiness: From the murder of Uriah and the others who were slain with him, 2Sa 11:17.
open thou my lips: By giving me opportunity to praise you, when you will forgive my sins.
broken spirit: Which is a wounding of the heart, proceeding from faith, which seeks God for mercy.
Zion: He prays for the whole Church, because through his sin it was in danger of God's judgment.
righteousness: That is, just and lawful, applied to the right end, which is the exercise of faith and repentance.
